A motorcycle shifting in its lane is usually not a mistake by the rider, but a response to something on the road ahead. You will learn how heavy and long these vehicles can be, why you should never cut in front of one, how to use the mirror test to tell whether a driver can see you, and what the No-Zone is. You will also learn why riding alongside or tailgating a large vehicle is dangerous, and how to finish a pass safely. Large vehicles cannot stop, turn or see the way cars can, so most of the responsibility for safe spacing falls on the drivers of the smaller vehicles around them. Make it part of your routine on every trip.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-F09","sec05-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":43,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Size and weight","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Up to eighty thousand pounds.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R12"]},{"text":"Longer than ninety feet.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R12"]},{"text":"Doubles and triples longer still.","fact_ids":["sec05-F07","sec05-R12"]}],"narration":{"text":"A typical tractor-trailer can weigh as much as eighty thousand pounds, and with a long trailer the whole rig can be longer than ninety feet. On busy intercity routes, double and triple trailer rigs can run longer than one hundred feet. That size affects everything: how long the vehicle takes to stop, how much room it needs to turn, and how much damage it can do in a crash. When you share the road with a vehicle that large, give it plenty of room and never assume it can react to you as quickly as a car would. If you need to turn off the road soon, stay behind the truck rather than slipping in front of it. Waiting a few seconds behind a truck is always safer than putting your car in the space a heavy vehicle needs to stop. Think ahead, and you will rarely be surprised.","fact_ids":["sec05-F08"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":44,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"The No-Zone","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Blind spots beside, behind and in front.","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]},{"text":"Mirror test: see the driver?","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]},{"text":"Stay out unless truly necessary.","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]}],"narration":{"text":"The No-Zone is the set of blind spots beside, behind and in front of a truck or bus where a car disappears from the driver's view. A simple test tells you if you are in one: if you cannot see the truck or bus driver in that vehicle's rearview mirrors, the driver cannot see you either. Stay out of the No-Zone unless it is truly necessary. Do not ride alongside a large vehicle for long stretches, and do not tailgate one. Keep a safety cushion around it, so the driver can see you and has room to move. Patience here is always the safer choice.","fact_ids":["sec05-F10","sec05-F09","sec05-F11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":42,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec05-u02-s5","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Finishing the pass","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F08"]},"lines":[{"text":"Wait to see the cab in your mirror.","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F08"]},{"text":"Signal and keep your speed.","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F08"]},{"text":"Never slow down ahead of it.","fact_ids":["sec05-F12","sec05-F08"]}],"narration":{"text":"Here is the trap. Wait until you can see the truck's cab in your rearview mirror before you move back in. Then signal, hold your speed, and do not slow down in front of it. Slowing right after cutting back in is especially dangerous, because the truck needs far more distance to stop than you do. On a test, the correct cue for returning to the lane is seeing the cab in your mirror. It tells you the truck driver cannot see you either, because you are in one of the blind spots that make up the No-Zone. You should move out of it, either by passing promptly when it is safe or by dropping back, until you can see the driver in the mirror. Do not ride alongside the truck for long. It may shift through ten gears to reach the speed limit, and its engine moves thirty to forty times the weight a car engine does. So a truck pulling away from a stop or merging takes time to reach traffic speed.
